process_area.title: Building Automation, Energy Control & Facilities Analytics

value_stream.name: Integrated Facilities Management, Workplace Services & Building Automation

fields.Volume: ~205 sites × BMS/IoT (HVAC, lighting, energy meters, sensors)

Automation Opportunity: - IoT auto-monitoring/alerting; BMS-data auto-ingest to analytics; predictive-maintenance from sensor data
Controls: - CTL-646 (ensure controlled execution — Building Automation, Energy Control & Facilities Analytics (PA-138.3).)
- CTL-646: BMS OT-security assessed/segmented (VS-27.3); platform governed (VS-113)
Cross-references: - links to VS-120 (energy), VS-27.3 (OT security), VS-113 (EA), VS-28 (analytics), VS-20.2 (engineering), VS-37 (new-site BMS)
Pain Points / Risks: - **OT-security risk**: BMS/IoT exposed to cyber-attack (building hijack); mitigated by OT security (VS-27.3) and segmentation
- **Integration-debt risk**: Proprietary siloed BMS per site; mitigated by architecture standards (VS-113)
System Touchpoints: - BMS/IoT platform; energy monitoring (VS-120); OT security (VS-27.3); analytics (VS-28); EA standards (VS-113)

steps.activity: Facilities/IT/EA define the BMS/IoT architecture and standards (controllers, protocols, IoT sensors, central monitoring) for stores/DCs/HQ, integrated with the energy program (VS-120)
Facilities/IT deploy the BMS at sites (HVAC/lighting/meter control, environmental sensors), connect to central monitoring, and secure it (OT security links to VS-27.3)
Facilities/Energy operate the BMS (monitoring, alarms, control), integrate data into analytics (VS-28/VS-120), and maintain the platform lifecycle (W4168-style governance)

fields.Trigger: Energy-efficiency program (VS-120); comfort complaint; optimization cycle

Automation Opportunity: - Occupancy-aware auto-control; set-point-override alerts; energy-vs-comfort optimization algorithms
Controls: - CTL-646: HVAC/lighting optimization balanced with comfort (VOC); savings measured (VS-120 M&V)
Cross-references: - links to VS-120 (energy/EEC), VS-25 (ESG/decarbonization), VS-13 (customer comfort), VS-83 (staff wellness), W4185 (BMS)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Comfort-sacrifice risk**: Over-optimizing energy harms comfort/sales; mitigated by comfort/Efficiency balance and VOC monitoring
- **Set-point-drift risk**: Manual overrides undo optimization; mitigated by BMS control + override alerts
System Touchpoints: - BMS control (W4185); energy M&V (VS-120); customer/staff comfort (VS-13/VS-83); ESG/decarbonization (VS-25)

steps.activity: Facilities/Energy optimize HVAC/lighting schedules and set-points via the BMS (occupancy-aware, time-of-day, tropical-climate tuning), aligned to the energy-conservation plan (VS-120.2)
Facilities/Store Ops balance comfort vs efficiency (customer/staff comfort links to VS-13 VOC, VS-83 wellness), and tune environmental control (humidity, ventilation) for tropical conditions
Facilities/Energy measure HVAC/lighting energy savings vs baseline (links to VS-120 M&V W3747), report to EEC governance (VS-120), and feed into decarbonization (VS-25)

fields.Participants: Real Estate (VS-97), Store Ops (VS-07), PMO (VS-112), IT (VS-99)
fields.Volume: HQ (~3,000 sqm) + DC office space + back-office

Automation Opportunity: - Occupancy-sensor analytics; desk/room-booking automation; utilization dashboards
Controls: - CTL-646 (ensure controlled execution — Building Automation, Energy Control & Facilities Analytics (PA-138.3).)
- CTL-646: space register reconciled with real estate (VS-97); changes coordinated via PMO (VS-112)
Cross-references: - links to VS-97 (real estate), VS-27 (booking/sensors), VS-99 (IT moves), VS-109 (remodel), VS-112 (PMO), VS-134 (OCM)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-utilization risk**: Paying for unused space; mitigated by utilization measurement and consolidation
- **Disruption risk**: Poorly-managed moves disrupt work; mitigated by PMO coordination (VS-112) and OCM (VS-134)
System Touchpoints: - Space/occupancy register; booking/occupancy sensors (VS-27); real estate (VS-97); IT moves (VS-99); remodel (VS-109)

steps.activity: Facilities maintain the space/occupancy register (HQ/DC office, workstations, meeting rooms, storage) integrated with real estate (VS-97) and plan-vs-actual utilization
Facilities measure space utilization (occupancy sensors, desk/room booking links to VS-27), identify under/over-utilized space, and recommend reconfiguration/consolidation
Facilities execute space changes (reconfig, moves links to VS-99 IT equipment moves, remodel links to VS-109), and report utilization/savings (W4192)

fields.Participants: ESG (VS-25), Energy (VS-120), Waste (VS-73), Green-Building Advisory (VS-78), HSE (VS-24)
fields.Trigger: Sustainability strategy (VS-25); green-building target; certification cycle
fields.Volume: ~205 sites (green operations, water, waste, materials, IEQ)

Automation Opportunity: - Sustainability-KPI dashboards; water/waste/materials auto-tracking; certification evidence automation
Controls: - CTL-646 (ensure controlled execution — Building Automation, Energy Control & Facilities Analytics (PA-138.3).)
- CTL-646: sustainability claims backed by measured KPIs (VS-25); certification evidence retained (VS-88)
Cross-references: - links to VS-25 (ESG), VS-25.1/VS-25.3 (environmental/reporting), VS-73 (waste), VS-120 (energy), VS-78 (green-building advisory), VS-88 (records)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Greenwashing risk**: Claims unsupported by performance; mitigated by measured KPIs and certification
- **Cost-benefit risk**: Green initiatives without ROI; mitigated by business-case discipline (VS-133)
System Touchpoints: - ESG reporting (VS-25); waste (VS-73); energy (VS-120); green-building advisory (VS-78); BMS IEQ (W4185)

steps.activity: Facilities/ESG define green-building operations standards (water efficiency, waste diversion, sustainable materials, indoor environmental quality) aligned to ESG (VS-25) and green-building advisory (VS-78)

Facilities operate green programs (water recycling, LED retrofits, waste diversion links to VS-73, low-VOC materials, IEQ monitoring) and pursue/retain certification (BERDE/LEED EBOM where applicable)
Facilities/ESG measure sustainability performance (water/waste/materials/IEQ KPIs), report to ESG (VS-25.1/VS-25.3), and support green-building advisory (VS-78) for clients

fields.Participants: Engineering (VS-20.2), Procurement (VS-34), Finance (VS-17.4), Store Ops (VS-07), Contractors
fields.Trigger: Minor capex (below VS-40 threshold); reconfiguration; facility upgrade
fields.Volume: Many small facilities projects across ~205 sites

Controls: - CTL-646 (ensure controlled execution — Building Automation, Energy Control & Facilities Analytics (PA-138.3).)
- CTL-646: minor-works budget/scope controlled (VS-112); safety/permits (VS-24/VS-22); quality close-out
Cross-references: - links to VS-112 (PMO), VS-40 (capex), VS-34 (procurement), VS-22 (permits), VS-24 (safety), VS-109 (remodel), VS-20.2 (engineering)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Scope-creep risk**: Minor works balloon; mitigated by defined scope/budget and PMO discipline (VS-112)
- **Disruption risk**: Construction disrupts trading; mitigated by off-hours scheduling and Store Ops coordination
System Touchpoints: - PMO/PMIS (VS-112); capex (VS-40); procurement (VS-34); permits (VS-22); remodel (VS-109); HSE (VS-24)

steps.activity: Facilities scope the minor-works project (re-paint, re-roof, fit-out, system upgrade below capex threshold links to VS-40), build the business case, and route approval
Facilities/Procurement source the contractor (links to VS-34), execute with minimal operational disruption (coordinate with Store Ops/DC), and manage safety/permits (VS-24/VS-22)
steps.r: Facilities Project Lead / Contractor / Store Ops

steps.activity: Facilities/PMO close out (quality, cost, handover W4190), capture lessons, and feed major works into capex (VS-40) or remodel (VS-109)

fields.Participants: Store Opening (VS-37), Real Estate (VS-97/VS-20), Engineering (VS-20.2), IT (VS-99), HSE (VS-24)
fields.Trigger: New store opening (VS-37); DC opening; site closure (VS-59)

Automation Opportunity: - Commissioning-checklist automation; warranty/O&M digital handover; permit-readiness tracking
Controls: - CTL-646 (ensure controlled execution — Building Automation, Energy Control & Facilities Analytics (PA-138.3).)
- CTL-646: commissioning checklist complete; fire-safety/occupancy permit before opening (VS-22.1); O&M/warranty handover
Cross-references: - links to VS-37 (store opening), VS-20.2 (construction/engineering), VS-97 (real estate), VS-22.1 (permits), VS-59 (closure), VS-24.2 (emergency procedures), W4171 (service catalog)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Incomplete-handover risk**: Site opens with unfinished/non-compliant systems; mitigated by commissioning checklist and permit gate
- **Closure-risk**: Abandoned/secured site liabilities; mitigated by decommission procedure (VS-59)
System Touchpoints: - Store opening (VS-37); construction (VS-20.2); real estate (VS-97); permits (VS-22.1); BMS (W4185); closure (VS-59)
Time Estimate: - Per opening (weeks of commissioning); per closure per VS-59

steps.activity: Facilities commission building systems at handover (HVAC, fire/life-safety, electrical, plumbing, BMS, elevators) and verify against design/spec, coordinating with construction (VS-20.2) and store opening (VS-37)
Facilities onboard services (cleaning, pest, guarding, grounds, waste, utilities) to the new site per the service catalog (W4171), and obtain fire-safety/occupancy permits (VS-22.1)
Facilities/Store Opening hand over to site ops (O&M manuals, warranties, BMS training, emergency procedures VS-24.2); for closure (VS-59), decommission/securing/salvage

fields.Participants: BCP (VS-26), HSE (VS-24.2), IT (VS-27), LP (VS-23), Store Ops (VS-07)
fields.Volume: ~205 sites × critical systems (power, fire, security, HVAC, water)

Automation Opportunity: - Critical-system IoT health monitoring; failover auto-test; BCP scenario automation
Controls: - CTL-646 (ensure controlled execution — Building Automation, Energy Control & Facilities Analytics (PA-138.3).)
- CTL-646: critical-system resilience designed & tested (VS-26); emergency procedures drilled (VS-24.2)
Cross-references: - links to VS-26 (BCP), VS-26.1/VS-26.2 (BCP testing/response), VS-69 (typhoon/disaster), VS-24.2 (emergency), VS-23 (security), W4185 (BMS)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Single-point-of-failure risk**: No backup for a critical system; mitigated by resilience design and failover testing
- **Slow-recovery risk**: Disaster recovery unprepared; mitigated by BCP testing (VS-26.1) and emergency procedures (VS-24.2)
System Touchpoints: - BCP (VS-26); emergency response (VS-24.2); disaster (VS-69); BMS alarms (W4185); work-orders (W4174)

steps.activity: Facilities/BCP identify critical building systems per site (power/generator, fire/life-safety, security, key HVAC, water) and their failure impact, aligned to BCP (VS-26.1)
Facilities ensure resilience (generator backup, fire-system redundancy, BMS fail-safe, spare-parts stock, provider SLA) and test failover periodically (links to VS-26.1 BCP testing)
Facilities respond to critical-system failure/disaster (typhoon VS-69, fire, flood, outage) per emergency procedures (VS-24.2/VS-26.2), recover, and capture lessons

fields.Participants: Analytics (VS-28), Finance (VS-17.4), OpEx (VS-133), Store Ops (VS-07), Providers
fields.Trigger: Monthly/quarterly review; OpEx cycle; benchmark refresh

Automation Opportunity: - Facilities-KPI dashboards; process-mining on work-order data; benefit-realization automation
Controls: - CTL-646 (ensure controlled execution — Building Automation, Energy Control & Facilities Analytics (PA-138.3).)
- CTL-646: facilities KPIs reviewed monthly; improvements benefit-tracked (VS-133); cost-to-serve benchmarked
Cross-references: - links to VS-28 (analytics), VS-133 (OpEx), VS-17.4 (finance), VS-112 (PMO), VS-13/VS-103.2 (satisfaction), VS-120 (energy KPI), W4176 (cost-to-serve)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Metric-blindness risk**: Operating without facilities KPIs → drift; mitigated by monthly analytics
- **No-realization risk**: Improvements not measured; mitigated by benefit-realization tracking (VS-133)
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (VS-28); OpEx/process mining (VS-133); finance (VS-17.4); PMO (VS-112); satisfaction (VS-13/VS-103.2)

steps.activity: Facilities/Analytics measure facilities KPIs — SLA adherence (W4171), PM-vs-reactive ratio (W4173/W4174), cost-to-serve (W4176), uptime, energy (VS-120), customer/employee satisfaction (VS-13/VS-103.2)
Facilities/OpEx identify improvement opportunities (recurring issues, cost leakage, process variants) via analytics/process mining (VS-133), and prioritize with benefit modeling
Facilities execute improvement projects (links to VS-133/VS-112), track benefit realization (VS-133 W4065), and benchmark facilities cost-to-serve vs retail norms
